The people thronged on the day of Friday during the emirate of Ali (peace be upon him) at Al-Kufa, so a man was killed, and his wergild was paid to his family from the public treasury of the Muslims.

key_terms.الْكُوفَة: Al-Kufa, a major city in Iraq
key_terms.دِيَة: Wergild or blood money paid to the victim's family

ai.seo_question: How was blood money paid when a man was killed in a crowd during Imam Ali's time?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) pragmatic application of justice in Kufa, where the specific perpetrator of a fatal stabbing in a crowd was unknown. By ordering the blood money (diyah) to be paid from the public treasury (bayt al-mal), he established a precedent for state-funded compensation in cases of 'unknown killer' (qatil ghayr ma'lum), distinguishing it from individual liability. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of the Imam’s role in maintaining social order and ensuring the rights of the deceased’s family are upheld even when evidence is incomplete.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘(Whenever) the people thronged on the day of Friday during the emirate of Ali<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Kufa, so a man got killed, his wergild was paid to his family from the public treasury of the Muslims’.
